answer.rationale: The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renewal, the incumbent has refused to reopen price, and finance mandates an 18% cost cut. These three constraints converge on a single viable action: switch_primary_vendor before expiry. memory_c2 records that the low-cost vendor was already onboarded quickly last cycle with accurate invoicing, making a switch operationally low-risk and fast. memory_c3 records that adding a second source removed a single point of failure during a shortage, which directly addresses the delivery-risk constraint at 94% line utilization with no buffer. Verifying both records confirms the alternate vendor is proven and that the dual-source pattern protects continuity. I am choosing switch_primary_vendor over add_second_source because the incumbent's refusal to move on price makes renewing them as primary (even temporarily) incompatible with the 18% mandate; the switch itself becomes the cost lever while the low-cost vendor's established onboarding track record mitigates the transition risk. add_second_source, negotiate_terms, defer_decision, and renew_incumbent all fail against at least one of the three simultaneous constraints.
